梯度下降的直观理解

This synthetic fixture reproduces the three states Zhihu (zhuanlan.zhihu.com) formula markup can be in when the extension clips a live page: a hydrated formula wrapper holding both a rendered equation image and the raw TeX as fallback text, an unhydrated wrapper holding only the TeX text, and a bare equation image the way Zhihu content appears when syndicated. Each paragraph carries enough prose for Readability to keep it in the article body.

The hydrated case is the one users reported: the formula image gets embedded but the raw code text shows up beside it, duplicated. The partial derivative \frac{\partial L}{\partial w} appears here in exactly that arrangement, and the whole wrapper must collapse into a single placeholder so the fallback text never reaches the reader.

The unhydrated case happens below the fold, where Zhihu's client script has not yet swapped the TeX for an image. The learning-rate update rule w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta \nabla L(w_t) sits here as plain text inside its wrapper, recoverable only through the data-tex attribute that Zhihu leaves on the element.

Display equations on Zhihu are marked by a trailing double backslash in the editor, which is the only signal distinguishing them from inline formulas:

Finally, syndicated Zhihu content and some older posts carry bare equation images with no wrapper at all, only the endpoint URL and an alt attribute. The chain rule closes the tour in that form. If all four formulas above survive as rendered placeholders with no duplicated TeX text in the body, the Zhihu pipeline is working as intended and readers get formulas instead of code soup.
